title: First Apron Level definition and annual scaling
summary: How the First Apron Level dollar amount is set each Salary Cap Year.
detail_paraphrase: For 2023-24, the First Apron Level equals the 2023-24 Tax Level plus $6.716 million scaled by a fraction (numerator = average of the 2022-23 and 2023-24 Salary Caps; denominator = the 2022-23 Salary Cap). For every later Salary Cap Year, the First Apron Level is the 2023-24 First Apron Level multiplied by (that year's Salary Cap divided by the 2023-24 Salary Cap). For these calculations the Salary Cap is taken under Sections 2(a)(1)-(3) without the 2(a)(5)/(6) adjustments.
conditions: Applies for each Salary Cap Year during the term of the Agreement
applies_to: all teams (defines the threshold)
thresholds: 2023-24: Tax Level + ($6.716M fixed dollar base, scaled by cap-growth fraction); later years: 2023-24 First Apron Level x (year cap / 2023-24 cap)
notes: The $6.716M is a fixed dollar base; the rest scales with the cap.

title: Second Apron Level definition and annual scaling
summary: How the Second Apron Level dollar amount is set each Salary Cap Year.
detail_paraphrase: For 2023-24, the Second Apron Level equals the 2023-24 Tax Level plus a fixed $17.5 million. For every later Salary Cap Year, the Second Apron Level is the 2023-24 Second Apron Level multiplied by (that year's Salary Cap divided by the 2023-24 Salary Cap). For these calculations the Salary Cap is taken under Sections 2(a)(1)-(3) without the 2(a)(5)/(6) adjustments.
conditions: Applies for each Salary Cap Year during the term of the Agreement
applies_to: all teams (defines the threshold)
thresholds: 2023-24: Tax Level + $17.5M (fixed dollar base); later years: 2023-24 Second Apron Level x (year cap / 2023-24 cap)
notes: The $17.5M is a fixed dollar base; it then scales with the cap in later years.

title: Apron Team Salary definition
summary: The salary figure measured against the apron levels for transaction restrictions.
detail_paraphrase: Apron Team Salary is a Team's Team Salary adjusted by several add-backs and subtractions: plus all Performance Bonuses excluded under Section 3(d); plus the salary of a 0-or-1-year-of-service free agent contract under Section 2(d)(1)(i)(F); plus any amount that could be added under Section 4(a)(1)(iii); minus Free Agent Amounts under Section 4(a)(2); plus, for a Restricted Free Agent, the greater of the salary plus Unlikely Bonuses in any outstanding Qualifying Offer / Maximum Qualifying Offer or in any First Refusal Exercise Notice; minus amounts for unsigned First Round Picks under Section 4(a)(4); plus any outstanding Required Tender to a First Round Pick; minus any Salary Cap Exception deemed included under Sections 4(a)(7) and 6(n)(2); plus any amount excluded under Section 4(l); and minus any incomplete-roster cap-hold added under Section 4(f).
conditions: Used to test all apron-based transaction restrictions and hard caps
applies_to: all teams (defines the measured salary)
notes: Apron Team Salary, not raw Team Salary, is what the apron thresholds test against.

title: Core apron transaction-restriction and hard-cap mechanic
summary: How engaging in a listed transaction both blocks it above the relevant apron and hard-caps the team there for the rest of the year.
detail_paraphrase: For the transactions listed in the Transaction Restrictions Table (Section 2(e)(4)), two rules apply at any point in a Salary Cap Year: (A) a Team may not engage in a listed transaction if, immediately afterward, its Apron Team Salary would exceed the Applicable Apron Level shown for that transaction; and (B) once a Team engages in a listed transaction, it may not, for the rest of that Salary Cap Year, have an Apron Team Salary exceeding that Applicable Apron Level. Rule (B) is the hard-cap trigger: the team is hard-capped at the first or second apron (whichever the table assigns) for the remainder of the year.
conditions: A transaction listed in the Transaction Restrictions Table is proposed or completed
exceptions: 2023-24 partial carve-out for rows F through J under Section 2(e)(5) - see APRON-021
applies_to: all teams (mechanic); hard-caps the team at the apron tied to the transaction
thresholds: Hard cap set at the Applicable Apron Level (first or second apron) tied to the transaction
notes: This is the central engine; individual transactions and their apron tiers are itemized in APRON-006 through APRON-016.

title: Post-Regular-Season look-ahead restriction for rows E through J
summary: Offseason transactions in rows E-J are also tested against next year's apron.
detail_paraphrase: During the period from the day after a Regular Season's last day through the end of that Salary Cap Year, in addition to the same-year rules, rows E through J of the Transaction Restrictions Table are also tested against the immediately following (Subsequent) Salary Cap Year: a Team may not do such a transaction if its projected Subsequent-year Apron Team Salary would exceed that year's Applicable Apron Level, and once done it may not exceed that level at any time through the end of the Subsequent year. Section 2(e)(3) specifies the assumptions used to project the Subsequent-year Apron Team Salary (all team/player options exercised, no ETOs exercised, no further current-year transactions, Higher Max Criteria assumed met where applicable, and current-year cap/apron amounts used as a stand-in for next year's).
conditions: Transaction in rows E-J
Occurs after the last day of the Regular Season through the end of that Salary Cap Year
applies_to: all teams (offseason look-ahead for rows E-J)
thresholds: Projected Subsequent-year Apron Team Salary must not exceed the Subsequent-year Applicable Apron Level
notes: Effectively extends the hard cap into the following season for qualifying offseason trade-exception moves.

title: First apron: Bi-annual Exception (Table row A)
summary: Signing or acquiring a player with the Bi-annual Exception is barred above the first apron and hard-caps at the first apron.
detail_paraphrase: Row A: a Team signing or acquiring a player using the Bi-annual Exception (Section 6(d)) may not do so if its Apron Team Salary would then exceed the First Apron Level, and once used the team may not exceed the First Apron Level for the rest of the year. In effect, teams over the first apron cannot use the Bi-annual Exception, and a team that uses it is hard-capped at the first apron.
conditions: Team signs or acquires a player using the Bi-annual Exception
applies_to: teams at or above the first apron (forbidden); using it hard-caps at the first apron
thresholds: First Apron Level

title: First apron: Non-Taxpayer Mid-Level Salary Exception (Table row B)
summary: Using the Non-Taxpayer MLE is barred above the first apron and hard-caps at the first apron.
detail_paraphrase: Row B: a Team signing or acquiring a player using the Non-Taxpayer Mid-Level Salary Exception (Section 6(e)) may not do so if its Apron Team Salary would then exceed the First Apron Level, and is hard-capped at the First Apron Level for the rest of the year once it uses the exception.
conditions: Team signs or acquires a player using the Non-Taxpayer Mid-Level Salary Exception
applies_to: teams at or above the first apron (forbidden); using it hard-caps at the first apron
thresholds: First Apron Level
notes: The Non-Taxpayer MLE is worth up to 9.12% of the Salary Cap (Section 6(e)(1)).

title: First apron: acquiring a sign-and-trade player (Table row C)
summary: Acquiring a player on a contract signed-and-traded under Section 8(e)(1) is barred above the first apron and hard-caps at the first apron.
detail_paraphrase: Row C: a Team acquiring a player pursuant to a contract entered into under Section 8(e)(1) (a sign-and-trade of a Veteran Free Agent) may not do so if its Apron Team Salary would then exceed the First Apron Level, and is hard-capped at the First Apron Level for the remainder of the year. This is the standard sign-and-trade acquisition hard cap.
conditions: Team acquires a player via a Section 8(e)(1) sign-and-trade contract
applies_to: teams at or above the first apron (forbidden); acquiring hard-caps at the first apron
thresholds: First Apron Level
notes: Refers to Section 8(e)(1) sign-and-trade; the acquiring team is the one hard-capped.

title: First apron: re-signing a terminated above-MLE contract during the season (Table row D)
summary: Re-signing a buyout/terminated player whose prior salary exceeded the Non-Taxpayer MLE is barred above the first apron and hard-caps at the first apron.
detail_paraphrase: Row D: during the Regular Season, a Team signing a player who was previously under a contract that (i) was terminated during that Regular Season and (ii) before termination provided a salary for the encompassing Salary Cap Year greater than the Non-Taxpayer Mid-Level Salary Exception amount, may not do so if its Apron Team Salary would then exceed the First Apron Level, and is hard-capped at the First Apron Level afterward. This is the 'buyout-market' restriction targeting waived players who were earning above the Non-Taxpayer MLE.
conditions: In-season signing of a player whose prior, in-season-terminated contract paid more than the Non-Taxpayer MLE for that year
applies_to: teams at or above the first apron (forbidden); signing hard-caps at the first apron
thresholds: First Apron Level; prior-contract salary threshold = the Non-Taxpayer MLE amount for that Salary Cap Year (a % of cap base)
notes: This is the bought-out-player signing limit commonly cited as a buyout-market restriction.

title: First apron: Expanded Traded Player Exception (Table row E)
summary: Acquiring a player via the Expanded TPE is barred above the first apron and hard-caps at the first apron.
detail_paraphrase: Row E: a Team acquiring a player using an Expanded Traded Player Exception (Section 6(j)(1)(iv)) may not do so if its Apron Team Salary would then exceed the First Apron Level, and is hard-capped at the First Apron Level afterward. The Expanded TPE lets non-aproned teams take back substantially more salary than they send out (up to roughly 200% / +$7.5M-scaled / 125% formulas), so teams over the first apron lose access to it.
conditions: Team acquires a player using the Expanded Traded Player Exception
applies_to: teams at or above the first apron (forbidden); acquiring hard-caps at the first apron
thresholds: First Apron Level
notes: Expanded TPE is the high-take-back matching exception; the apron tier here is the first apron.

title: First apron: Standard Traded Player Exception used in later/offseason window (Table row F)
summary: Acquiring a player via a Standard TPE used after the season in which it arose is barred above the first apron and hard-caps at the first apron.
detail_paraphrase: Row F: a Team acquiring a player using a Standard Traded Player Exception (Section 6(j)(1)(i)) (i) after the end of the Regular Season in which that TPE arose, or (ii) if the TPE arose in the offseason window, after the last day of the following Regular Season, may not do so if its Apron Team Salary would exceed the First Apron Level, and is hard-capped at the First Apron Level afterward. This is the prior-year (carried-over) TPE-use restriction for the standard, non-aggregated trade exception.
conditions: Team uses a Standard Traded Player Exception
Use occurs after the Regular Season in which the TPE arose (a carried-over / prior-year TPE)
applies_to: teams at or above the first apron (forbidden); using it hard-caps at the first apron
thresholds: First Apron Level
notes: Only the carried-over (prior-year) use is restricted; using a Standard TPE within the season it arose is not in this table row.

title: First apron: Transition Traded Player Exception (Table row G)
summary: Acquiring a player via the Transition TPE is barred above the first apron and hard-caps at the first apron.
detail_paraphrase: Row G: a Team acquiring a player using a Transition Traded Player Exception (Section 6(j)(1)(iii)) may not do so if its Apron Team Salary would exceed the First Apron Level, and is hard-capped at the First Apron Level afterward. The Transition TPE exists only during the 2023-24 Salary Cap Year.
conditions: Team acquires a player using the Transition Traded Player Exception
Available only in 2023-24
applies_to: teams at or above the first apron (forbidden); using it hard-caps at the first apron
thresholds: First Apron Level
notes: Transition TPE is a one-time 2023-24-only exception (Section 6(j)(1)(iii)).

title: Second apron: Aggregated Standard Traded Player Exception (Table row H)
summary: Aggregating salaries in a trade (Aggregated Standard TPE) is barred above the second apron and hard-caps at the second apron.
detail_paraphrase: Row H: a Team acquiring a player using the Aggregated Standard Traded Player Exception (Section 6(j)(1)(ii)) - i.e., combining two or more outgoing contracts to match an incoming one - may not do so if its Apron Team Salary would exceed the Second Apron Level, and is hard-capped at the Second Apron Level afterward. In effect, a team over the second apron cannot aggregate salaries in a trade.
conditions: Team aggregates two or more outgoing contracts using the Aggregated Standard Traded Player Exception
applies_to: teams at or above the second apron (forbidden); using it hard-caps at the second apron
thresholds: Second Apron Level
notes: This is the well-known 'no aggregating salaries above the second apron' rule.

title: Second apron: paying cash in a trade (Table row I)
summary: Sending cash to another team in a trade is barred above the second apron and hard-caps at the second apron.
detail_paraphrase: Row I: a Team paying cash to another Team in connection with a trade under Section 8(a) may not do so if its Apron Team Salary would exceed the Second Apron Level, and is hard-capped at the Second Apron Level afterward. Teams over the second apron cannot include outgoing cash in trades.
conditions: Team pays cash to another team in a trade under Section 8(a)
applies_to: teams at or above the second apron (forbidden); paying cash hard-caps at the second apron
thresholds: Second Apron Level
notes: Restricts only paying cash out; the general cash-in-trade limit (5.15% of cap) is separate - see APRON-019.

title: Second apron: TPE acquisition tied to a sign-and-traded contract (Table row J)
summary: Using any TPE to acquire a player whose contract was signed-and-traded under Section 8(e)(1) is barred above the second apron and hard-caps at the second apron.
detail_paraphrase: Row J: a Team acquiring a player using any Traded Player Exception (Section 6(j)(1)(i)-(iv)) where that TPE is in respect of a Player Contract signed and traded under Section 8(e)(1) may not do so if its Apron Team Salary would exceed the Second Apron Level, and is hard-capped at the Second Apron Level afterward.
conditions: Team uses a Traded Player Exception
The TPE relates to a Section 8(e)(1) signed-and-traded contract
applies_to: teams at or above the second apron (forbidden); using it hard-caps at the second apron
thresholds: Second Apron Level
notes: Distinct from row C: row C is acquiring the sign-and-trade player directly; row J is using a TPE generated by such a contract.

title: Second apron: Taxpayer Mid-Level Salary Exception (Table row K)
summary: Signing a player with the Taxpayer MLE is barred above the second apron and hard-caps at the second apron.
detail_paraphrase: Row K: a Team signing a player using the Taxpayer Mid-Level Salary Exception (Section 6(f)) may not do so if its Apron Team Salary would exceed the Second Apron Level, and is hard-capped at the Second Apron Level afterward. Thus a team over the second apron loses even the Taxpayer MLE, and a team that uses the Taxpayer MLE is hard-capped at the second apron.
conditions: Team signs a player using the Taxpayer Mid-Level Salary Exception
applies_to: teams at or above the second apron (forbidden); using it hard-caps at the second apron
thresholds: Second Apron Level; Taxpayer MLE itself = $5M (2023-24) scaled by cap thereafter, usable only if Apron Team Salary then exceeds the First Apron Level
notes: Row K is the only signing exception assigned to the Second Apron Level. Note the Taxpayer MLE itself is only usable when the team is above the First Apron Level (Section 6(f)(1)).

title: Above-first-apron teams lose the Expanded Traded Player Exception take-back room
summary: The Expanded TPE's higher take-back is unavailable to teams that would exceed the first apron after the trade.
detail_paraphrase: The Expanded Traded Player Exception (Section 6(j)(1)(iv)) permits take-back of the greater of roughly 200% (+$250K) capped against a 100%+$7.5M-scaled alternative, or 125% (+$250K) of outgoing salaries. Because row E ties its use to the First Apron Level, a team cannot use the Expanded TPE if doing so would push its Apron Team Salary above the First Apron Level, and using it hard-caps the team at the first apron. Above the first apron, teams are limited to the narrower Standard TPE take-back rather than the expanded matching room.
conditions: Team's post-trade Apron Team Salary would exceed the First Apron Level
applies_to: teams at or above the first apron
thresholds: First Apron Level; Expanded TPE take-back formulas: greater of (lesser of 200%+$250K or 100%+$7.5M-scaled) or 125%+$250K of outgoing salary
notes: Combines the Section 6 take-back math with the row-E apron tie; this is the 'can't take back more salary than you send' consequence above the first apron.

title: Sign-and-trade acquisition requires Room and is apron-restricted
summary: A Section 8(e)(1) sign-and-trade is subject to apron rules and the acquiring team must have Room for the first-year salary.
detail_paraphrase: A Veteran Free Agent and his Prior Team may sign a contract for the purpose of trading it (sign-and-trade) only if conditions in Section 8(e)(1) are met, including: the player finished the prior season on the Prior Team's roster; the contract is 3-4 seasons (excluding any option year); it is not signed via the Non-Taxpayer MLE or Room MLE; the first season is fully protected for lack of skill; it is entered into before the first day of the Regular Season; certain max-salary limits for 5th-Year-Eligible players; and the acquiring Team has Room for the player's first-season salary plus Unlikely Bonuses. This whole mechanism is expressly subject to the Section 2(e) apron rules, which is why acquiring such a player (row C) hard-caps the acquirer at the first apron.
conditions: Veteran Free Agent signs with Prior Team under agreement to trade
All Section 8(e)(1) conditions met
depends_on_terms: Mid-Level Salary Exception for Room Teams
applies_to: teams at or above the first apron (acquisition forbidden); acquiring hard-caps at the first apron
thresholds: Acquiring team must have Room for first-season salary; first apron hard cap on acquirer
notes: The acquiring team's Room requirement plus the row-C first-apron hard cap is the practical sign-and-trade restriction.

title: General cash-in-trade limit (separate from the second-apron cash ban)
summary: All teams have an annual cash-in-trade cap of 5.15% of the Salary Cap; second-apron teams additionally cannot pay any cash out.
detail_paraphrase: Subject to Section 2(e), a Team may pay or receive in trades during a Salary Cap Year up to an aggregate 5.15% of that year's Salary Cap in cash across all such trades (including reimbursements for acquired players' compensation). Amounts paid and received are not netted against each other. This is the league-wide cash cap; it is distinct from the row-I second-apron rule that forbids a second-apron team from paying out any cash at all.
conditions: Team pays or receives cash in one or more trades during a Salary Cap Year
exceptions: Second-apron teams face a stricter zero-out-cash limit under row I - see APRON-014
applies_to: all teams (general cash cap)
thresholds: 5.15% of the Salary Cap (a % base) per Salary Cap Year, aggregate; paid and received not netted
notes: Included because the second-apron cash ban (APRON-014) sits on top of this general limit.

title: Taxpayer MLE prior use blocks later first-/second-apron transactions same year
summary: A team that has signed a contract with the Taxpayer MLE this year is barred from certain table-row transactions for the rest of that year.
detail_paraphrase: Additional restrictions apply to teams that use the Taxpayer Mid-Level Salary Exception: in 2023-24, a Team may not engage in any transaction in rows A through E of the Transaction Restrictions Table if it has already signed a contract using the Taxpayer MLE that year. Beginning with 2024-25, that prohibition expands to rows A through F. This prevents combining the Taxpayer MLE with the broader exception/trade tools listed in those rows within the same Salary Cap Year.
conditions: Team has previously signed a player using the Taxpayer Mid-Level Salary Exception in the same Salary Cap Year
applies_to: teams that have used the Taxpayer MLE (effectively above the first apron)
thresholds: 2023-24: blocks rows A-E; 2024-25 onward: blocks rows A-F
notes: Functions as a one-way hard restriction once the Taxpayer MLE is used.

title: 2023-24 carve-out: rows F through J do not impose a 2023-24 hard cap
summary: In 2023-24 only, using rows F-J transactions does not by itself bar exceeding the applicable apron that year.
detail_paraphrase: Notwithstanding the general mechanic, a Team engaging in one or more rows F through J transactions during the 2023-24 Salary Cap Year is not, by virtue of those transactions alone, prohibited from having a 2023-24 Apron Team Salary above the Applicable Apron Level for that year. (The pre-transaction test under 2(e)(2)(i)(A) and the offseason look-ahead still apply per the worked examples.)
conditions: Transaction in rows F-J
2023-24 Salary Cap Year only
applies_to: all teams (2023-24 transitional relief for rows F-J)
thresholds: Applies only to the 2023-24 Salary Cap Year
notes: One-year transition rule; the (B)-style remainder-of-year hard cap from those rows is suspended for 2023-24.

title: Second Apron Team definition (draft-pick penalty trigger)
summary: A team is a Second Apron Team if its Apron Team Salary exceeds the Second Apron Level as of its last Regular Season game.
detail_paraphrase: A 'Second Apron Team' for a Salary Cap Year is a Team whose Apron Team Salary, measured as of the start of the Team's last Regular Season game that year, exceeds the Second Apron Level for that year. This status is the trigger for the first-round draft-pick freeze and Draft Pick Penalty rules.
conditions: Apron Team Salary exceeds the Second Apron Level as of the start of the team's last Regular Season game
applies_to: teams above the second apron
thresholds: Second Apron Level, measured at the start of the team's last Regular Season game
notes: Timing of measurement (last Regular Season game) is what fixes Second Apron Team status.

title: Second Apron Team frozen draft pick (cannot trade the seven-years-out first-rounder)
summary: A Second Apron Team is barred from trading its first-round pick seven seasons out.
detail_paraphrase: Beginning with the 2024-25 Salary Cap Year, if a Team is a Second Apron Team for a Salary Cap Year, it is prohibited (conditionally or unconditionally) from trading its first-round draft pick in the first NBA Draft occurring after the seventh season following the season within that Salary Cap Year. The pick is effectively frozen/un-tradeable.
conditions: Team is a Second Apron Team for the Salary Cap Year
2024-25 Salary Cap Year or later
exceptions: Pick may later become tradeable under the four-year look-forward test - see APRON-024
applies_to: teams above the second apron
thresholds: First-round pick in the draft following the seventh season after the relevant season
notes: The 'frozen' seven-years-out pick; distinct from the end-of-first-round Draft Pick Penalty in APRON-024.

title: Draft Pick Penalty for repeat Second Apron Teams (pick moves to end of round)
summary: If a team is a Second Apron Team in 2+ of the next four years, its frozen first-rounder is bumped to the last pick of the first round.
detail_paraphrase: For the four Salary Cap Years immediately following the year that froze the pick: (A) if the Team is a Second Apron Team in two or more of those four years, the frozen first-round pick is subject to a Draft Pick Penalty - it becomes the final pick of the first round regardless of the team's record (with ties among penalized teams broken by inverse winning percentage); (B) if the Team is a Second Apron Team in fewer than two of those four years, the pick is unfrozen (tradeable, no penalty) as of the day after the third of those four years in which the team is not a Second Apron Team.
conditions: A pick was frozen under APRON-023
Second Apron Team status evaluated over the next four Salary Cap Years
exceptions: Pick is freed and not penalized if the team is a Second Apron Team in fewer than two of the four years
applies_to: teams above the second apron (repeatedly)
thresholds: Penalty if Second Apron Team in >= 2 of the 4 following years; pick moved to last selection in the first round
notes: Draft Pick Penalty is the 'pick drops to 30th' consequence for repeat second-apron teams.

title: Standard TPE $250,000 buffer eliminated above the first apron
summary: The $250K trade-matching allowance drops to $0 if the post-trade Apron Team Salary would exceed the first apron.
detail_paraphrase: Notwithstanding the Traded Player Exception take-back formulas, if a Team's post-assignment Apron Team Salary would exceed the First Apron Level, the $250,000 allowance referenced in each of the Traded Player Exceptions (Sections 6(j)(1)(i)-(v)) is reduced to $0. Above the first apron, teams lose the small extra cushion on incoming salary in trades.
conditions: Post-assignment Apron Team Salary would exceed the First Apron Level
applies_to: teams at or above the first apron
thresholds: First Apron Level; $250,000 allowance reduced to $0
notes: A further take-back tightening for above-first-apron teams beyond losing the Expanded TPE.
